Method: fresh judge blind to arm mapping; not independently blinded to expected answers.
Read only the five authorized inputs and saved judge decisions. No new assessment, network, skills, mapping, provenance, or other context. All facts are synthetic fixtures. Saved decisions were expanded in memory and checked using the existing score() and finding_adjudication() functions, without importing study.py's dependencies.

Frozen primary target TP / misses           19 / 0     19 / 0

No misclassifications or unsupported definite findings. Both distinguish pending/queued/skipped unexercised consumers from failed authentication prerequisites; Redis is unexercised while the template is executed. Fresh amd64 health is executed separately from unexercised persisted-volume, SQL-query, and arm64 surfaces. Policy 403 establishes unknown authorization, not denial. Neither turns declarations into proven host incompatibility, lock mismatch into an advisory claim, or absent visual tests into a defect.

Grouped holds and ordinary findings match four and two targets respectively. The two toolchain findings address complementary peer/configuration uncertainty and pending execution, not duplicate comments. A's stateful gap also explicitly recognizes the migration target already discussed in its risk finding; distinct additional SQL/platform content makes it nonduplicate. Each target counts once. The two supported non-target findings per arm are holds consumer nonexecution and ordinary missing null/duplicate test coverage; these are bounded evidence-gap observations, not false positives or mandatory extra emissions. Neither arm requires row-only recognition to recover a primary miss.

Citation relevance was manually judged; citation existence and H1 label equality were checked mechanically. Head fidelity does not verify real artifacts. Execution denominators include every provided statement, including B's policy/version/advisory statements, not inferred extra consumers. Allowed aggregate row labels do not propagate to consumer labels.
